title: Remove Duplicates From a Sorted List

concept.title: Skip a node by changing one pointer
body: Deleting a node from a linked list does not move any data: you make the **previous node point to the node after it**. In a sorted list, equal values stand next to each other, so you only need to compare a node with its successor. If they are equal, cut the successor out with `cur.next = cur.next.next`. Do **not** move `cur` in that case: the new successor may be equal too.
The first node of every group of equal values stays, so the head of the list never changes here.

statement: A singly linked list is sorted in non-decreasing order. Delete the duplicates so that every value appears only once, and print the resulting list.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, the number of nodes. The second line has the values of the nodes, from the head to the tail. The values are in non-decreasing order.
outputFormat: Print the values of the new list on one line.
hints: Equal values are neighbours, because the list is sorted.
If a node and its successor are equal, set `cur.next = cur.next.next`.
Move to the next node only when the successor is different.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

# Every node is also remembered in this list. Python in the browser cannot free a very long chain of nodes at once,
# so free_nodes() (called at the end) cuts the links first and the nodes are then freed one by one.
all_nodes = []


class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next
        all_nodes.append(self)


def free_nodes():
    for node in all_nodes:
        node.next = None
        if hasattr(node, "random"):
            node.random = None
    all_nodes.clear()


# Builds a list from the values. If pos is 0 or more, the last node points back to the node at index pos (a cycle).
def build_list(values, pos=-1):
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = ListNode(v, head)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        for _ in range(pos):
            target = target.next
        tail.next = target
    return head


# Prints the values of a list on one line ("empty" for an empty list).
def print_list(head):
    out = []
    while head is not None:
        out.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
    print(*(out if out else ["empty"]))

a = list(map(int, input().split()))

print_list(delete_duplicates(build_list(a)))

explanation: A node whose successor has the same value is bypassed by changing one pointer. The reference only moves on when the successor is different.
